issues.description: The problem statement contains conflicting return-type specifications for messageOnMilk(): the UML fragment and descriptive text in the problem claim it should return a boolean (true/false) while other UML fragments and all template/solution code treat messageOnMilk() as returning a String message. This contradiction will confuse students about the correct method signature to implement and which value to return (a boolean success flag vs. a printable message).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type for messageOnMilk() consistent across the problem statement, UML, and examples. Since the template and solution use/expect a printable message and the Main template prints m.messageOnMilk(), update the problem statement (both the UML and the descriptive text) to specify messageOnMilk(): String and replace references to returning true/false with guidance describing the expected milking message (e.g. "Seal <name> is milked"). Alternatively, if a boolean return was intended, change the template and solution examples to use a boolean signature and adjust code that prints the result accordingly. Preferably align the problem statement to match the existing template/solution (String) to avoid breaking student code expectations.

issues.description: The method messageOnMilk() is described in the problem statement (UML and text) as returning a boolean (true/false depending on milking success), but the solution implements Milkable.messageOnMilk() and concrete classes (Seal, Goat) to return a String. This mismatch of the same conceptual method across artifacts creates confusion about the expected signature and return value for students.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the expected signature of messageOnMilk() across the problem statement, template, and solution. Either (A) update the problem statement to state messageOnMilk() returns a String (and show example messages) so it matches the solution's Milkable interface and implementations, or (B) change the solution to have messageOnMilk() return boolean and provide a separate method (e.g. milkMessage()) for the printable message. Ensure all artifacts (UML, textual description, template comments, and solution code) use the same signature.
